name: Setu Bandhasana
description: A supine backbend. Lying on the back with knees bent and feet planted, the hips lift until the body forms a straight ramp from shoulders through hips to knees. Best assessed from a side view.
camera_hint: Place your camera to your side, about 2-3 metres away, so your whole body is in frame from the side.
image_credit: Photo: Biswarup Ganguly / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY 3.0
benefits: Strengthens the glutes, hamstrings and back
Opens the chest and front of the hips
A gentle backbend accessible to most beginners
cues: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat, hip width apart
Place your feet close enough that your fingertips can graze your heels
Press through your feet and lift your hips
Keep your knees pointing forward, not splaying outward
Keep your neck relaxed and your gaze straight up

feedback.low: Your heels are tucked in very tightly. Slide your feet slightly further from your hips.
feedback.high: Walk your feet closer to your hips so your knees bend toward a right angle.

feedback.high: Walk your feet closer to your hips so your knees bend toward a right angle.
Lift your hips higher to make one straight line from your shoulders through your hips to your knees.

feedback.low: Press through your feet and lift your hips higher off the floor.

feedback.high: Bring your feet back so your ankles sit directly under your knees.
Your knees are splaying outward. Draw them back to hip width and keep them parallel.
